about.title: Personal Injury Help in Dana Point, California
about.longDescription: Dana Point may be known for its harbor views, but its roads carry plenty of everyday traffic risk. Public records show 81 injury collisions in the most recent final year, leaving 107 people hurt and 3 people dead. Corridors like Pacific Coast Highway, Rt 1, Stonehill Drive, and the stretch of I-5 that runs through the area account for a large share of these reported crashes, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing the heaviest concentration. If you or someone close to you was hurt in one of these incidents, the days and weeks after can feel overwhelming — medical visits, insurance calls, missed work, and uncertainty about what comes next. We're here to help injured people in Dana Point review what happened and understand the options available. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Reaching out costs nothing and starts the process of finding real answers.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney After an Injury

items.title: You Have Two Years — But Not Forever
items.desc: California generally gives injured people two years from the date of the incident to file a claim. Claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months, so it helps to act sooner rather than later.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible for what happened. Any award is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Actually Suffered
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in most ordinary injury cases. That means the full extent of your experience can be considered, not just medical bills.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost. Fees only come out of a settlement or award if one is reached.

items: Worrying about medical bills piling up while you can't work

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an injury in Dana Point?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the incident to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity, like a city or county vehicle, was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months for filing a notice of claim. It's best to speak with an attorney as soon as possible to avoid missing a deadline.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. We can help assess how fault might be divided in your specific situation.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Dana Point?
items.answer: Public collision records show that corridors like Pacific Coast Highway, Rt 1, Stonehill Drive, and the local stretch of I-5 account for a notable share of reported injury collisions, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing higher counts. These are simply neutral public-record figures, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact us?
items.answer: No. There's no charge to discuss your situation with us or find out whether we can help with your case.

items.question: Will I owe attorney fees if my case doesn't result in a settlement?
items.answer: We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. If there's no settlement or award, you generally owe no attorney fee for our work on the case.
